standard_prerequisites.name: Serre duality on the Cohen-Macaulay curve
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same unit, Situation situation-Cohen-Macaulay-curve and the duality of Section section-Riemann-Roch
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof reduces H^1(X, omega_X tensor L) = 0 to H^0(X, L^{tensor -1}) = 0 by the duality discussed in the Riemann-Roch section.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1353-1359): in the Cohen-Macaulay curve situation, if L is a globally generated invertible O_X-module not isomorphic to O_X, then H^1(X, omega_X tensor L) = 0.
Duality reduction (proof lines 1361-1364): by duality it suffices to show H^0(X, L^{tensor -1}) = 0.

Generator argument (lines 1365-1368): if t is a nonzero global section of L^{tensor -1}, then because L is globally generated some global section s of L satisfies st is nonzero - otherwise t would vanish on every member of a generating family of global sections and hence be zero.
Contradiction (lines 1368-1369): st lies in H^0(X, O_X) = k and is a nonzero constant, so s is a nowhere-vanishing section of the invertible sheaf L, whence L cong O_X, contradicting the hypothesis.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the dual vanishing statement by duality.
Derive a nonzero pairing product from global generation.
Conclude the line bundle is trivial, contradicting the hypothesis.
difficulty_reason: Vanishing lemma (statement 1353-1359, proof 1361-1369): a globally generated non-trivial invertible sheaf has no twisted dualizing H^1 - the proof is the duality reduction plus the standard generator pairing argument; two short steps are compressed in the source (the existence of s with st nonzero, and the trivialization by a nowhere-vanishing section) but their mechanisms are the standard generator and trivialization arguments, transparent from the span. H2: short duality argument with compressed standard steps.
